commands.name: artefact-visuel
commands.description: Construire un artefact visuel pour Alexis (explication, comparaison, plan, diagnostic, chose à montrer, maquettes) avec le kit de composants maison, sans réécrire de CSS, et avec choix + commentaire renvoyés à Claude depuis la page. Use quand un schéma, des cartes ou une ligne du temps rendraient une réponse plus claire que des phrases (mécanisme, comparaison d'options, plan, diagnostic, chiffres, chose à montrer), quelle que soit sa longueur, avant de coder un nouvel écran ou un nouveau bloc visible (maquettes), ou quand il demande un artefact. (user)

commands.name: banque-design
commands.description: Goûts design validés d'Alexis et banque de sites qu'il a notés. Use avant de concevoir ou refaire un site, une landing page, un écran d'app, un style de démo de la ferme ou des maquettes ; et quand Alexis dit avec ses mots qu'un site, une app ou un design lui plaît ou lui déplaît (l'ajouter à la banque). (user)

commands.name: break-ui
commands.description: Casser un écran ou un composant avec les pires données réalistes (nom à rallonge, email sans coupure, adresse interminable, prénom d'une lettre, champ manquant, 0 / 1 / 1 000 éléments, montant énorme, emoji), derrière un interrupteur Démo / Pire cas réservé au dev, puis lister ce qui casse avec la correction de chacun. Use when Alexis demande de stress-tester ou casser un écran, de chercher les cas limites d'un composant, ou de « tester le pire cas » — VTC Planner Mobile ou Desktop, un site, une démo de la ferme. Pour le goût, l'animation ou la critique d'interface, c'est ui-craft. (user)

commands.name: commit
commands.description: Commit automatique tout-en-un. Stage, commit, push, et merge feature si applicable. Zero confirmation. (user)

commands.name: cua-driver
commands.description: Drive a native GUI app (macOS, Windows, Linux) via the cua-driver CLI (default) or MCP server; snapshot its accessibility tree, act through snapshot-bound element tokens, native menu paths, exact window geometry, or pixel coordinates, and verify from fresh state. Use when the user asks you to operate, drive, automate, or perform a GUI task in a real application on the host, or to continue, resume, or recall recent Cua activity. (user)

commands.name: m
commands.description: Merge le worktree courant (ou nommé) dans sa branche d'origine enregistrée puis nettoie tout. Use when l'utilisateur a fini de bosser dans un worktree et veut le rapatrier/merger/finaliser, ou tape /m [nom]. (user)

commands.name: motion
commands.description: Créer une vidéo marketing verticale VTC Planner (9:16, 60 i/s) avec le moteur maison HTML/Chrome/ffmpeg (dossier VTC-Planner\Motion), sans Remotion : une fonction ou nouveauté racontée en une scène 3D continue, mise en scène tirée au sort, musique synthétisée, puis légendes et publication via /publish. Use quand l'utilisateur veut une nouvelle vidéo de promo, un motion, « une vidéo sur telle fonction », ou tape /motion. (user)

commands.name: motion-design-remotion
commands.description: Professional motion design principles and battle-tested Remotion patterns for studio-quality promo videos (animation principles, anti-jitter layering, looping shimmers, app mockup choreography). Use when building or polishing a Remotion video, when text jitters or blurs during transforms, or when a video feels static or amateur. Complements the official remotion-best-practices skill (API usage) with the "why does it look pro" layer. (user)

commands.name: ntfy
commands.description: Publier ou brancher une notification ntfy (serveur auto-hébergé ntfy.ariasolutions.fr, topic Notifications pour l'iPhone ou Journal pour le Cockpit seul, choix de la priorité, création d'un utilisateur write-only). Use quand un script, un service, un hook ou un cron doit envoyer une notification push à Alexis, ou quand on touche à un producteur ntfy existant. (user)

commands.name: pentest
commands.description: Orchestrated offensive pentest of web domains and their hosting infrastructure. Runs recon → network/service scan (nmap: ports, FTP/SSH/SMTP/DB) → web fingerprint/TLS/wpscan → targeted exploitation → dir/subdomain/auth fuzzing, then writes a timestamped Markdown report with severity, confidence and fix. Use when the user wants to pentest, scan or attack their own site/server/infra, mentions nmap/recon/ports/FTP/services/vulns/brute-force/fuzzing against their domains, or types /pentest <target>. Authorized targets only — enforce the allowlist. (user)

commands.name: publish
commands.description: Publish or schedule ANY ready media (video or image) on VTC Planner's social networks (TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube) via the social-upload CLI — immediately or on the next optimal planning slot. Use when the user runs /publish <media path>, wants to post/republish a video or image outside a /remotion campaign, or asks to add a ready file to the social planning. For a full feature campaign (video creation + captions + publish), use /remotion instead. (user)

commands.name: rappel
commands.description: Programmer un email de rappel à Alexis (user@example.com) pour une date future, sans attendre qu'il le demande, dès qu'une tâche laisse une échéance, une vérification à faire plus tard, un résultat à lire, un essai ou un abonnement à résilier, ou une relance. Use quand un chantier laisse une date à surveiller, ou quand Alexis demande un rappel. (user)

commands.name: remotion
commands.description: Generate a full VTC Planner marketing campaign for a newly shipped app feature — a 9:16 promo video (animated feature slides + the canonical CTA slide) whose per-screen visuals are validated up front via preview stills, plus per-platform French captions with hashtags, then publish it autonomously via the social-upload CLI (immediately or scheduled on the optimal weekly planning). Use when the user runs /remotion (optionally with a feature name/keyword as argument) to announce a new app feature on social (TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube). Reconstructs the real RN screen on an iPhone mockup using the house brand charter. (user)

commands.name: remotion-best-practices
commands.description: Best practices for Remotion - Video creation in React (user)

commands.name: review-maison
commands.description: Revue de code plafonnée à 6 agents (5 chercheurs, 1 vérificateur), cadrage fait par la session. Lancée uniquement par /review-maison [cible]. (user)

commands.name: s
commands.description: Supprime un worktree créé par /w comme s'il n'avait jamais existé — AUCUN merge, branche jetée (-D), junction retirée, projet Arkadia fermé, rien poussé. Use when l'utilisateur veut abandonner/jeter un worktree d'essai qui ne lui plaît pas, ou tape /s [nom]. Pour rapatrier le travail, c'est /m, pas /s. (user)

commands.name: seo-audit
commands.description: When the user wants to audit, review, or diagnose SEO issues on their site (technical SEO, on-page SEO, meta tags, "why am I not ranking", SEO health check). (user)

commands.name: ui-craft
commands.description: Bonnes pratiques design/animation d'Emil Kowalski (animations.dev, animate-expo) + Apple Fluid Interfaces, adaptées React Native/Reanimated ET web/CSS. Use when créer ou modifier de l'UI, une animation, une transition, un geste, un modal/sheet, un feedback tactile (press/haptique), un état de chargement, de la typographie, un parcours (retour arrière, écran de confirmation) ou un libellé de bouton — sur VTC Planner Mobile, Desktop, le site, une page web ou une démo de la ferme à sites. Aussi pour critiquer une interface, reviewer du code UI, choisir easing/durée/spring, diagnostiquer une animation qui saccade sur un vrai téléphone ou dans un navigateur, ou quand un site web « fait site » sur téléphone (survol collé, flash au tap, zoom sur un champ, encoche, 100vh, carrousel). (user)

commands.name: vtc-planner-assets
commands.description: The VTC Planner house brand charter — apply to EVERY user-facing/visual VTC Planner surface, in any medium. Use whenever creating or restyling a VTC Planner visual or brand-facing artifact: social post, story/reel, promo video, app mockup, website / landing page, marketing email, transactional email, App Store / Play Store screenshot, banner, or PDF. Defines the canonical tokens (premium gold palette, Sora/Inter, light premium aesthetic) and routes to the right engine per medium. Never start a VTC Planner visual from a generic style. (user)

commands.name: w
commands.description: Crée un worktree git isolé en frère du repo principal, node_modules partagé par junction Windows (aucun npm install), merge-back via /m. Use when l'utilisateur veut un espace de travail parallèle isolé ou tape /w <nom>. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: claude-security:scan
commands.description: Claude Security scan pipeline: inventory, threat-model, research and sweep over a codebase, or a review of one change; then a three-lens adversarial panel and a code-computed tally (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: frontend-design:frontend-design
commands.description: (frontend-design) Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.

commands.name: superpowers:brainstorming
commands.description: (superpowers) You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, modifying behavior, or planning anything new, in software or out of it (a talk, a business, a renovation).

commands.name: superpowers:diagnosing-superpowers
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when a superpowers session went wrong and your human partner wants to know why — repeated work, ignored plans, stumbles, poor results, a skill that didn't fire, "it took too long", "why is it so expensive", "what is it doing" — or wants to build a bug report for the superpowers maintainers, for the current session or a past one identified by id or path, on any harness.

commands.name: superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies

commands.name: superpowers:executing-plans
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when executing an implementation plan in the current session as the implementer yourself — your human partner chose inline execution, or no subagent tool is available

commands.name: superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work

commands.name: superpowers:receiving-code-review
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation

commands.name: superpowers:requesting-code-review
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements

commands.name: superpowers:subagent-driven-development
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session

commands.name: superpowers:systematic-debugging
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes

commands.name: superpowers:test-driven-development
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

commands.name: superpowers:using-git-worktrees
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback

commands.name: superpowers:using-superpowers
commands.description: (superpowers) Overview of how superpowers skills are organized. Load only when the user asks about superpowers itself. (neutralized-by-user)

commands.name: superpowers:verification-before-completion
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

commands.name: superpowers:writing-plans
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code

commands.name: superpowers:writing-skills
commands.description: (superpowers) Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:a11y-debugging
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Uses Chrome DevTools MCP for accessibility (a11y) debugging and auditing based on web.dev guidelines. Use when testing semantic HTML, ARIA labels, focus states, keyboard navigation, tap targets, and color contrast.

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:chrome-devtools
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Uses Chrome DevTools via MCP for efficient debugging, troubleshooting and browser automation. Use when debugging web pages, automating browser interactions, analyzing performance, or inspecting network requests. This skill does not apply to `--slim` mode (MCP configuration).

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:chrome-devtools-cli
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Use this skill to write shell scripts or run shell commands to automate tasks in the browser or otherwise use Chrome DevTools via CLI.

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:debug-optimize-lcp
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Guides debugging and optimizing Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) using Chrome DevTools MCP tools. Use this skill whenever the user asks about LCP performance, slow page loads, Core Web Vitals optimization, or wants to understand why their page's main content takes too long to appear. Also use when the user mentions "largest contentful paint", "page load speed", "CWV", or wants to improve how fast their hero image or main content renders.

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:memory-leak-debugging
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Diagnoses and resolves memory leaks in JavaScript/Node.js applications. Use when a user reports high memory usage, OOM errors, or wants to analyze heapsnapshots or run memory leak detection tools like memlab.

commands.name: chrome-devtools-mcp:troubleshooting
commands.description: (chrome-devtools-mcp) Uses Chrome DevTools MCP and documentation to troubleshoot connection and target issues. Trigger this skill when list_pages, new_page, or navigate_page fail, or when the server initialization fails.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:ask-matt
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:diagnosing-bugs
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:grill-with-docs
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:triage
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:improve-codebase-architecture
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:setup-matt-pocock-skills
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:tdd
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:to-spec
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:to-tickets
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:wayfinder
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:implement
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:implement-spec
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Implement the result of /to-spec and /to-tickets in code.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:prototype
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:research
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:codebase-design
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:code-review
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:pr
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Use when writing a PR body.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:retro
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:wizard
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:grill-me
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:grilling
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:handoff
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.
commands.argumentHint: What will the next session be used for?

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:teach
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.
commands.argumentHint: What would you like to learn about?

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:to-questionnaire
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:wait-what
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

commands.name: mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents
commands.description: (mattpocock-skills) Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

commands.name: claude-security:claude-security
commands.description: (claude-security) Claude Security: scan the codebase (the whole repository or a scoped part of it), scan changes (this branch's or a pull request's diff, or one commit), or suggest patches (findings turned into targeted patch files, each verified by a panel of agents, that you apply when you choose). Use when the user asks to scan, audit or check code with Claude Security, to scan their changes with Claude Security, or to fix or patch Claude Security findings.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: send-to-project
commands.description: Send this session's work to a Claude Project

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X".
